parts.title: The Warning Signs
parts.text: Nisha was the **anchor** of her research team — the one person everyone depended on to stay calm when the news was bad. Every morning she would **hoist** her heavy bag of notebooks onto her shoulder and read the latest climate data, her hands steady even as the numbers grew worse. It took real **courage** to stand up at the town meeting and tell people the truth: the coast was in danger, and they had very little time to act.

parts.title: The Crisis
parts.text: A massive storm stripped away the top **layer** of soil along the shoreline, and the flooding that followed became a **menace** to the whole town. Amara, who had come to the region years ago as a young **immigrant** and made it her home, knocked on every door urging her neighbors not to give up. Kiran's **role** as community leader had never felt heavier — she needed to keep everyone **steady** while the river rose around them.

parts.title: Taking Action
parts.text: The damage from the floods was not **modest** — it ran deep into the foundations of homes and lives. But Nisha believed there was a **reward** waiting for anyone willing to work for it: a safer, greener coast protected by mangrove trees. "Anyone who bothers to look will **stumble** upon research proving mangroves can reduce flood damage by half," she told the council. "I must **confess** I was skeptical at first, but the evidence is undeniable."

parts.title: A Greener Future
parts.text: Three years later, the mangrove forest stretched along two miles of coastline. When the next big storm came, the town survived with minimal damage. Kiran told the newspapers, "Nisha saved our town. She showed us that one person with a good idea can change everything." The town became a model for climate resilience, and Nisha's story was taught in schools across the country.
